name: Greenheart

stars.name: Greenheart
stars.notes: One of the oldest known stars hosting a complex biosphere. Its extreme age and stability have permitted evolutionary experiments found nowhere else in cataloged space.

planets.name: Char
planets.notes: Airless, sun-blasted rock with a surface of fused regolith. Mineral surveys indicate thorium deposits of potential commercial value.

planets.name: Primeval
planets.notes: Ancient garden world with the most biodiverse ecosystem in known space. Over 40 million cataloged species and an estimated 200 million total. Population 42 million in minimal-footprint research communities.

planets.name: Siltwaters
planets.notes: Desiccated world with trace atmospheric water vapor. Fossilized stromatolites confirm microbial life existed here billions of years ago.

planets.name: Frostcap
planets.notes: Frozen outer world with a thick nitrogen atmosphere and methane lakes. Prebiotic chemistry in the lakes is actively studied by remote probes.

planets.name: Outreach
planets.notes: Distant ice body serving as the system's outer communications relay point. Automated station maintains deep-space links.

anomalies.name: The Chorus
anomalies.notes: A persistent low-frequency harmonic detectable across Primeval's surface, generated by the combined metabolic activity of billions of organisms. Intensity correlates with seasonal biological productivity. Some researchers describe it as the planet singing.

asteroid_belts.name: The Old Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Ancient asteroid belt with heavily weathered surfaces. Isotopic dating places some fragments among the oldest solid material in the local stellar neighborhood.

stations.name: Primeval Gate
stations.notes: Primary access point to the system. All visitors must pass through extensive biosecurity and receive briefings on non-interference protocols before surface descent is authorized.

stations.name: The Archive
stations.notes: Xenobiology data repository and genetic library containing samples from over 12 million of Primeval's cataloged species. Considered one of the most valuable scientific collections in existence.

faction_control.notes: Scientific custodial governance with the strictest ecological protections in known space. Population caps, development bans, and mandatory impact assessments govern every human activity in the system.

history: First surveyed in 2303, initial biosignature analysis suggested a biosphere of unprecedented complexity. Crewed expedition in 2308 confirmed Primeval as the most biodiverse world ever discovered.
The Greenheart Preserve Authority was established by unanimous interstellar vote in 2312, imposing the most restrictive conservation regime ever applied to a star system.
By 2320, only 20% of Primeval's estimated species had been cataloged, with new species discovered at a rate of approximately 50,000 per standard year—a pace that shows no sign of slowing.
description: Greenheart is a cathedral of life. Its ancient orange star has burned for over nine billion years, and in that immense span, the world of Primeval has become something unique in cataloged space: a planet where evolution has had so long to work that biodiversity defies comprehension. Every ecological niche is occupied, subdivided, and occupied again. Forests layer thirty deep, from subterranean root ecosystems through surface undergrowth to canopy, upper canopy, and aerial biomes where organisms that are neither plant nor animal drift on wind currents, photosynthesizing and hunting in equal measure. The planet hums with life—literally, as The Chorus attests.

Human presence on Primeval is deliberately invisible. Forty-two million people live in research settlements designed to leave no lasting mark on the landscape—elevated platforms, enclosed walkways, filtered waste systems that release nothing into the environment. The Preserve Authority enforces these standards with absolute rigor: a single contamination incident in 2316 resulted in the permanent closure of an entire research station and the sterilization of a square kilometer of forest. Scientists accept these conditions because Primeval offers what no other world can—a window into what billions of years of uninterrupted evolution can produce.

The Chorus is Greenheart's signature mystery. A low-frequency harmonic vibration pervading Primeval's surface, generated by the combined metabolic processes of the planet's biosphere—respiration, photosynthesis, decomposition, growth—all resonating together into a sound that sensitive instruments can detect from orbit. It rises and falls with seasons, strengthens during the equatorial growing season, and dims during polar winters. Some scientists insist it is merely an emergent acoustic phenomenon. Others, listening to recordings where the frequency modulates in patterns that seem almost deliberate, are not so sure. Primeval has had nine billion years to develop its voice. The question is whether anyone is speaking.
